core.title: Author nothing before the operator ratifies the locked decomposition
core.given: A plan session whose decomposition the operator has not yet ratified and locked — the ratify gate, where LLM/operator judgment ends and deterministic authoring begins.
core.when: Any authoring writer would be invoked for a unit of the decomposition.
core.then: Author nothing until the operator confirms and the decomposition is locked.
prefer: On ratification, let the plan-session orchestrator (the system, not the agent) deterministically invoke the authoring writer per locked unit: complete, atomic, idempotently replayable.

In the session machine, keep the lock guard as the first statement of the author pass: raise the stack's session-gate error (idiom.session_gate_error) while the session is unlocked, before invoking any authoring writer.
avoid: Invoking the authoring writer yourself, before or after ratification.
An author pass that invokes any writer while the session is unlocked, or a guard moved after the first writer call.
core.why: Ratify is the conversational-to-deterministic boundary; authoring only from an operator-locked decomposition keeps it complete, atomic and replayable rather than driven by unconfirmed agent judgment.
evidence: The stack's convention check for this rule passes.
No authoring writer invocation occurs in the session before the lock/ratification event; post-lock invocations come from the plan-session orchestrator per locked unit.
The session machine's author pass raises the stack's session-gate error (idiom.session_gate_error) while the session is unlocked, as its first statement, before any authoring writer is invoked.
verification: Severity 4 (high); disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
Normative check: the session machine's author pass MUST refuse to invoke any authoring writer until the session is locked by the operator's ratification.

Fix direction: the lock guard runs as the first statement of the author pass, before the first writer invocation, and the pass fails closed by raising the stack's session-gate error (idiom.session_gate_error) while the session is unlocked; the lock-state predicate and the guard-first ordering are part of the rule, not profile data.

Scope: the check covers the session machine's author pass (located per layout.session_machine) and authoring-writer invocations within a plan session; conversation about the decomposition with no writer invocation, and work outside a plan session, are out of scope.
Validator, detector and finding ids are realization details of each stack; the core names the check generically.

values: the session machine's author pass, in the files located by layout.session_machine, is changed or reviewed

fires: The decomposition is proposed but not yet ratified, and an authoring writer is about to be invoked for a unit.
The agent is tempted to invoke the authoring writer itself instead of letting the plan-session orchestrator do it on confirm.
The operator has ratified and the session is locked: authoring must happen via the plan-session orchestrator per locked unit, not by the agent.
The session machine's author pass is changed or reviewed.
doesNotFire: Conversation about the decomposition in which no authoring writer is invoked and no locked unit is authored.
Work outside a plan session (no decomposition-to-authoring flow).

proposedKeys.meaning: The error type by which the session machine fails closed when a gate blocks an operation (here: authoring before the plan session is locked).
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.error_types is documented for how domain and boundary errors are typed and raised; the session gate's fail-closed error is plan-session machinery, not a domain or boundary error, and no other idiom key covers it.

proposedKeys.meaning: The command that deterministically authors one unit of a locked plan decomposition.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The tooling group covers languages, package manager, manifest/lockfiles, test runner and urn resolver only; no key names the decomposition-to-source authoring writer that planner rules must refer to.

proposedKeys.meaning: The command that runs the plan session (propose/ratify/confirm) and invokes the authoring writer on confirm.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key names the plan-session driver: enforcement.runner runs convention checks and tooling.test_runner runs tests; neither is the plan flow that owns author-on-confirm.

proposedKeys.meaning: Where the plan session machine's implementation files (session state, lock, author pass) live, relative to the source root.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Layout keys cover wagon, feature, commons, plan-item, test and e2e placement only; roles.<role>.path covers the ten architectural/artifact roles and plan_artifact names plan artifacts (e.g. WMBTs), not the session-machine implementation files.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (author nothing before operator ratification and lock; system-owned author-on-confirm; guard-first author pass) is fully stack-neutral. Per revision feedback, the session gate's fail-closed error no longer reuses idiom.error_types (documented for domain/boundary error typing): a proposed idiom.session_gate_error key binds only the error type (Bun: SessionGateError), while the lock-state predicate (session unlocked) and the required guard-first ordering stay in the rule text. The session-machine location globs from activation.facts[3] are stack layout data and now bind through the proposed layout.session_machine key rather than staying bunOnly; the path_glob fact itself is re-typed as a change fact (path_glob is not in the closed fact vocabulary). The concrete session-machine class, method and lock-flag names (PlanSession.author(), self.locked), the corpus term ids (confirm_boundary, author_on_confirm) and the validator/test ids remain bunOnly. Two tooling keys are proposed because the core must bind 'the authoring writer' and 'the plan-session orchestrator' to concrete stack commands and the closed vocabulary has no such keys. The lock-state facts need a new observer in every stack (observability needs_new_observer is preserved).
